messages:
maria j: quick summary from today's profiling run on KV-cache quantization (INT8 / FP8) — tl;dr: substantial memory wins but decode latency and a few quality regressions on longer prefixes. asking for opinions on kernel fallbacks + whether we should enable online calibration by default.

maria j: experiment setup: A100/H100 batch=1-8 mixed seq lengths (16, 128, 1024), beam=1, model=redwood-v1-small-ish (decoder-only), baseline=fp16 kv, variants=int8-kv, fp8-kv, int4-kv (prototype). measured: tail P50/P95 latency, per-token throughput, GPU mem footprint, and token-level logprobs on 2 eval sets (wiki short/ long-dialog).

daniel (eng-runtime): can you paste the perf table?

maria j: pasted below (trimmed):
```
CONFIG            | GPU | MEM delta | P50(dec) | P95(dec) | ppl_delta | notes
fp16 (baseline)   | A100| 0%        | 12ms     | 30ms     | 0.0%      | ---
int8-kv           | A100| -42%      | 13.2ms   | 34.1ms   | +1.6%     | +10-18% latency on long seqs
fp8-kv            | A100| -38%      | 12.6ms   | 31.8ms   | +0.9%     | stable across short seqs, H100 better
int4-kv (proto)   | A100| -60%      | 16.8ms   | 48.2ms   | +4.5%     | quality hits, bad for decode
int8-kv           | H100| -40%      | 11.8ms   | 28.0ms   | +1.2%     | optimized kernel available
fp8-kv            | H100| -35%      | 11.5ms   | 27.5ms   | +0.6%     | best win/quality on H100
```

priya s: interesting that FP8 is almost as good as INT8 for memory and slightly better on quality. do we know where latency regressed for INT8? kernel choice?

maria j: dug into traces — regression is split across two things: 1) the INT8 KV gather/scatter kernel currently uses a fallback path that does extra copies for padding alignment (kernel int8_kv_v1). 2) quant/dequant on hot path when cache-miss triggers a per-step calibration conversion (we left a defensive quant step enabled). on H100 the int8 kernels are vectorized so the copy is smaller.

jeffc: any flame graphs?

maria j: small flame snippet (top functions):
```
decode_step -> kv_read(int8_kv_v1) [35%] -> dequantize (copy) [12%]
batching_manager -> merge_prefixes [8%]
kernel_launch_overhead [6%]
```

daniel (eng-runtime): so kernel selection matters a lot. we should add a fast-path kernel (int8_kv_v2) that avoids the extra memcopy for aligned keys and falls back only on misaligned cases. can we detect alignment cheaply at compile/load time?

maria j: yes — we can detect per-GPU dtype alignment and preferred layout at model load; then pick int8_kv_v2 if layout ok. fallback to fp16_kv when not. switching to v2 in a micro-run on A100 dropped P95 from 34.1ms -> 29.0ms (still +3ms vs fp16 but much closer).

priya s: calibration effects? you mentioned a defensive quant step. what about offline calibration (per-model static scale) vs online (per-request running stats)?

maria j: we tried three modes:
- static calibration: offline per-shard min-max + KL on calibration corpus (costs time once at model load).
- online per-step adjust: adaptive scale update on first N tokens of each session (adds overhead per-request).
- hybrid: static baseline + occasional correction if drift detected.
Results: static gives best throughput (no runtime cost) but worse tail quality on some dialog corpora (ppl +1.2%). online reduces quality gap (ppl +0.2%) but adds ~3-6% throughput overhead in our bench. hybrid hits sweet spot: small 1% throughput hit, quality ~+0.4%.

jeffc: does online calibration cause non-determinism across identical inputs (race on stats)?

maria j: yes, if multiple threads update shared scale we'd see small differences. we isolated per-session stats and then atomically commit global corrections only when stable to keep determinism. still, prefer static or hybrid for reproducibility.

daniel (eng-runtime): batching heuristics: noticed that when we have many short requests + a few long ones, KV reuse is high, but batch coalescing can hurt because merges create bigger combined seqs -> more KV ops and alignment overhead. any numbers?

maria j: microbench: mixed workload (90% seq16, 10% seq1024, batch window 20ms) — with aggressive coalescing P50 decode slightly better but P95 spiked ~22% due to long seq handling and repeated dequant/copy. turning on prefix-priority batching (favor grouping short-with-short) reduced P95 back down and kept memory wins.

priya s: decode quality — specific failure modes for INT8 KV? token drop / repeated tokens?

maria j: main issues are subtle: lower logits tail mass reduced, causing low-probability continuation to be pruned earlier. triggers on long-history prompts and low-temp sampling. int4 is catastrophic in some cases. FP8 kept logits much closer to FP16 baseline.

jeffc: recommended path for rollout? canary options?

maria j: proposal:
- default: enable FP8-KV on H100 and INT8-KV on nodes with verified int8_kv_v2 kernel (boot-time check).
- fallback: fp16_kv for any mismatches or misaligned buffers.
- calibration: hybrid mode with static per-model scales and optional server-level drift checks (configs: kv_quant.mode = hybrid, kv_quant.hybrid_threshold = 0.02).
- telemetry: add token-level KL/regression alerts and perf counters for dequant copies.

daniel (eng-runtime): +1 to telemetry. also add a microbenchmark job in ring CI that runs batch patterns (short-only, mixed, long-only) on each runtime image; fail the build if P95 regresses >5% vs baseline.

priya s: what about storage of cached KV in quantized form on disk for private infra? encryption/encoding concerns?

maria j: store quantized bytes (int8/uint8 or fp8 encodings) in snapshot; on load choose kernel based on host GPU. ensure KMS signs snapshots to avoid bit-rot issues. we should add a flag to force decode to fp16 at load to reproduce exact baseline.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist added: runtime/int8_kv_v2 kernel present check, kv_quant.mode default 'hybrid', monitoring job 'kv-quant-microbench' scheduled.

jeffc: action items?

maria j: short list:
1) daniel: implement int8_kv_v2 alignment-fastpath & boot-time detection (owner).
2) priya: add token-level KL telemetry + quality alerts to console (owner).
3) jeffc: add microbench CI job + perf gating (owner).
4) maria: run longer canary on H100 fleet with fp8-kv enabled (owner).

priya s: I'll sketch the console alert thresholds and a small eval set for long-history failure cases.

maria j: thanks all. if anyone has objections to the rollout plan speak now, otherwise i'll open the PRs and schedule the canary. :thumbsup:

jeffc: all good from me.

maria j: PRs opened: PR#4567 (int8_kv_v2), PR#4568 (telemetry), PR#4569 (ci job).
